summary: Structural mock-card audit of all 2,263 active Physics/Chemistry mock cards. Eight Chemistry multistage mark-plan cards manually shortened to single recall questions. Not exhaustive AQA content verification.

edited.oldFront: What three ideas must a six-mark lattice comparison link?
edited.oldBack: Ionic charge/radius → attraction; model-vs-Born–Haber discrepancies; anion polarisation → covalent character.
edited.newFront: What can a large Born–Haber versus perfect-ionic lattice enthalpy difference indicate?
edited.newBack: Significant covalent character in the ionic compound.

edited.oldFront: Outline a full six-mark reply to three false claims about Gibbs feasibility.
edited.oldBack: 1) Endothermic can be feasible if TΔS > ΔH. 2) ΔG < 0 need not be fast: high Ea. 3) Raising T helps if ΔS > 0, hinders if ΔS < 0.
edited.newFront: Does a negative ΔG guarantee a fast reaction?
edited.newBack: No. A high activation energy can make a feasible reaction very slow.

edited.oldFront: In a 5-mark Period 3 first-IE explanation, what must you include?
edited.oldBack: Increasing nuclear charge and near-constant shielding; Al 3p vs Mg 3s; P/S 3p orbital pairing and repulsion.
edited.newFront: Which two drops interrupt the general rise in first ionisation energy across Period 3?
edited.newBack: Mg to Al (3p electron) and P to S (3p electron pairing).

edited.oldFront: What must a full 4-mark molecular-shape explanation include?
edited.oldBack: Electron domains, lone-pair count, repulsion order, shape and approximate bond angle.
edited.newFront: What must you count first to predict a molecule's shape?
edited.newBack: Bonding regions and lone pairs around the central atom.

edited.oldFront: How should a four-mark ionic melting-point answer be built?
edited.oldBack: State giant ionic lattice, opposite-ion electrostatic forces, strong attractions, much energy.
edited.newFront: What must be overcome when an ionic solid melts?
edited.newBack: Strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions.

edited.oldFront: How should a four-mark bond-polarity comparison be built?
edited.oldBack: Identify polar bonds, δ charges, 3D shapes, then cancel/non-cancel bond dipoles.
edited.newFront: When can a molecule with polar bonds still be non-polar?
edited.newBack: When its bond dipoles cancel because of the molecule's shape.

edited.oldFront: How should you justify a lower bond angle in a 4-mark answer?
edited.oldBack: Count bond/lone pairs, compare repulsions, name shape and resulting reduced angle.
edited.newFront: Why is NH₃'s bond angle smaller than CH₄'s?
edited.newBack: NH₃ has a lone pair; its stronger repulsion reduces the bond angle.

edited.oldFront: Four-mark plan: why does one liquid hydrogen-bond more strongly?
edited.oldBack: Identify N/O/F–H bond, δ+ H, acceptor lone pair, and energy needed to separate molecules.
edited.newFront: When a hydrogen-bonded liquid boils, which bonds are overcome?
edited.newBack: Intermolecular hydrogen bonds, not covalent O–H or N–H bonds.
